query_text: how do you type up minutes of a meeting

parts.text:
Typing up meeting minutes is a crucial task that turns a discussion into an official record and an actionable plan. The secret to writing great minutes is focusing on **decisions and actions**, rather than trying to record every single word spoken. 

Here is a step-by-step guide, along with a reusable template, to help you type up professional meeting minutes.

---

### Step 1: Use a Standard Structure
Every set of minutes should follow a consistent format. A standard layout includes:
*   **Meeting Details:** Name of the meeting, date, time, and location (or video link).
*   **Attendees:** Who was present, who was absent, and who was the chairperson and note-taker.
*   **Approval of Previous Minutes:** A brief note confirming that the minutes from the last meeting were accepted.
*   **Agenda Items:** A summary of the discussion for each topic, major points raised, and decisions made.
*   **Action Items:** A clear table or list detailing what needs to be done, who is doing it, and by when.
*   **Next Meeting:** Date, time, and location of the next meeting.

---

### Step 2: Write with the Right Tone and Style
*   **Be objective:** Use neutral, professional language. Do not include personal opinions, emotions, or office politics (e.g., instead of *"John angrily argued that the budget was too small,"* write *"Concerns were raised regarding budget constraints"*).
*   **Use the past tense and third person:** Write "The board approved..." instead of "We approve..." or "The board approves...".
*   **Summarize, don’t transcribe:** Do not write down who said what word-for-word. Instead, summarize the main points of the debate and clearly state the conclusion.
*   **Reference attachments:** If a presentation or report was shared, simply refer to it in the text (e.g., *"As outlined in the Q3 Marketing Presentation (see Attachment A)..."*).

---

### Step 3: Format Action Items Clearly
The most important part of meeting minutes is the **Action Items**. If someone leaves a meeting not knowing what they are supposed to do, the meeting has failed. Always format action items using this formula:
> **[Task] — [Owner/Assignee] — [Deadline]**

*Example:* 
*   **Action:** Submit the final budget draft — **Sarah T.** — **By Oct 15**

---

### Step 4: Review and Distribute
*   **Type them up quickly:** Try to type and send the minutes within 24 hours of the meeting while the details are still fresh in your mind.
*   **Proofread:** Check for spelling, grammar, and correct names.
*   **Get approval:** If required, send the draft to the chairperson or meeting lead for approval before sending it to the wider group.
*   **Distribute:** Email the final PDF or link to all attendees and anyone who was absent but needs to be kept in the loop.

---

### Standard Meeting Minutes Template
You can copy and paste this template into Word, Google Docs, or an email:

```text
[ORGANIZATION/COMPANY NAME]
MEETING MINUTES

Meeting Name: 
Date: [DD/MM/YYYY]
Time: [Start Time] to [End Time]
Location: [Conference Room / Zoom Link]
Chairperson: [Name]
Note-taker: [Your Name]

1. ATTENDEES
Present: [Name 1], [Name 2], [Name 3]
Apologies (Absent): [Name 4]

2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES
The minutes of the previous meeting held on [Date] were reviewed and approved [with/without] amendments.

3. AGENDA ITEMS

Topic 1: [Insert Topic Name]
• Discussion: [Brief 2–3 sentence summary of the main points discussed.]
• Decision: [Clearly state what was decided or agreed upon.]
• Action Items: 
  - [Task 1] – Assigned to: [Name] – Deadline: [Date]

Topic 2: [Insert Topic Name]
• Discussion: [Summary...]
• Decision: [Decision...]
• Action Items:
  - [Task 2] – Assigned to: [Name] – Deadline: [Date]

4. OTHER BUSINESS (AOB)
• [Note any unexpected topics brought up at the end of the meeting]

5. NEXT MEETING
Date: [Date of next meeting]
Time: [Time of next meeting]
Location: [Location of next meeting]
```

### Pro-Tips for Success:
*   **Get the Agenda early:** If you have the agenda before the meeting starts, you can pre-type the template, meeting date, attendee list, and agenda headings. During the meeting, you’ll just have to fill in the blanks.
*   **Clarify decisions immediately:** If a discussion is winding down and a decision hasn't been clearly made, ask: *"Just to make sure I have this correct for the minutes, what is our final decision and who is taking ownership of the next step?"*
